newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed sharply higher on Tuesday after weaker than expected U.S. economic data triggered a strong afternoon rally in an already rising market.

"There was some relief after the release (of the data), and since then, it's been more or less status quo," one dealer said, adding the Bund future had not been able to hold above the resistance level of 101.
U.S. labour costs rose 0.6 percent in the first quarter, below market consensus of a 0.9 percent increase.
U.S. durable goods orders fell three percent in March, the largest drop since August last year, while April consumer confidence at 116.8 was also below the forecast 118.4.
"It was quite a big (bond price) rise, but the undelying cash volume wasn't that great compared to the number of futures changing hands," one dealer said.
Trade was active in the 30-year benchmark, which ended 89 basis points higher at 112.62/82, yielding 6.48 percent, and in several shorter maturities.
The very short bonds underperformed the market, causing the yield curve to flatten.

Many players, especially end-investors, were said to have held onto their money as they awaited other economic data due later this week to get more signs of possible inflationary pressures in the U.S.

"And tomorrow, the Dutch market will be closed (for Queen's Day, the national holiday). On Thursday, many European places will shut down (for Labour Day), while next Monday is a bank holiday for England," one trader said.
